beats.text: Years earlier, King Janaka was ploughing a field himself to prepare the ground for a sacred ritual.
Suddenly, the plough struck something hard in the soil.
From the earth emerged a glowing baby girl. Some tellings say she lay in a golden casket.
Janaka lifted her in his arms. He had no child of his own, and his heart filled with joy.
He named her Sita, meaning 'furrow.' Born of the Earth, she was raised as his own daughter, and loved by all of Mithila.
Later tellings say that as a girl, she once moved Shiva's bow aside like a toy while cleaning the room.
Janaka saw it and knew she was no ordinary child. Only a man who could string that same bow would be worthy of her.
